behavior: A `#render` slot can give the element of a part another `id` than the part gives. After the mount, each part that names that part names the `id` that the element has now, and follows each later change of it. This is true for the `aria-labelledby` of a group of Menu, Select or Combobox, of a toast, of `Slider.Root`, `Select.Trigger` and `Combobox.Trigger`, and for the `aria-describedby` of a toast. It is also true for the `aria-controls` of `NumberField.Increment` and `NumberField.Decrement`, which name the input, and of `Resizable.Handle`, which names its primary panel. While the element has an empty `id`, the other part has no such attribute. After the mount, a stepper of a root with no input has no `aria-controls`. A control of a field follows the same rule for its label and its messages. Base UI names the `id` prop of the part, or its generated id. A `render` element or a `render` function that gives the element another `id`, or an empty one, thus leaves a reference that names no element. Base UI has no Resizable.
